actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Seed of the environment's random generator
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

actions.description: Set the seed used by the simulated world's random number generators for subsequent steps, without resetting the world. The accepted seed is echoed in the receipt.

inputs.description: Seed used by the next reset
inputs.name: seed

facts.text: YertleEnv is a Gymnasium environment for the Yertle quadruped that loads simulation/yertle.urdf in PyBullet and exposes the standard Gymnasium API
YertleEnv subclasses gym.Env
The robot has 12 actuated joints: the four leg prefixes lf, rf, lb and rb times the three segments shoulder, thigh and shin
The action space is one residual per actuated joint: a Box with low -1.0 and high 1.0
The default action_scale is 0.4 rad
A step adds the scaled action residual to DEFAULT_STANCE and clips each target to the joint soft limits
The standing pose is shoulder 0.0, thigh -0.6 and shin 0.9 rad, repeated for the four legs
The per-joint soft limits are shoulder -45 to 45 degrees, thigh -90 to 20 degrees and shin 13 to 90 degrees
The observation space is a 48-dimensional Box of unbounded floats

The observation concatenates base linear velocity, base angular velocity, projected gravity, the velocity command, joint positions relative to the stance, joint velocities times 0.1 and the previous action
The default command ranges are vx 0.15 to 0.35 m/s, vy -0.1 to 0.1 m/s and yaw -0.4 to 0.4 rad/s
The simulation steps at 1/240 s and the control loop runs four physics steps per environment step (60 Hz), and an episode is 12 s
The maximum number of environment steps is int(episode_seconds / (sim_timestep * control_decimation))
A step sets truncated when the step count reaches the maximum
The termination thresholds are 0.08 m base height and 0.7 rad tilt (about 40 degrees)
A step reports terminated when the base height is below min_base_height or the tilt exceeds max_tilt
The reward uses exponential kernels for linear and yaw velocity tracking, a forward-progress term clipped to +-0.5 and penalties on energy, action rate, orientation and height
A fall subtracts 5.0 from the reward
reset(seed) replaces the numpy generator, samples a new velocity command, resets the joints to DEFAULT_STANCE and returns (observation, {})
Domain randomisation is on by default: base-mass scale 0.85 to 1.15, foot friction 0.6 to 1.2, observation noise 0.02 and random pushes every 150 steps of 0.25 m/s
The environment connects a PyBullet GUI client only when render_mode is human and a DIRECT (headless) client otherwise
render() returns a 640 by 480 RGB array when render_mode is rgb_array

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds the environment's generator before the command, mass, friction and observation noise are drawn; the packaged fake is deterministic for the same seed and actions, but it uses Python's random.Random while upstream uses numpy's default_rng, so one seed does not give the same values on the two implementations

gaps: rigid-body PyBullet dynamics including ground contact, foot friction, the position servo and the URDF inertia override: the fake models none of them

the fake's base velocity is a first-order stand-in for the sampled command, its joint motion is a first-order approach to the clipped targets and the robot never falls, so terminated is always false and only the default episode length truncates
the observation composition and the reward formula follow yertle_env.py, but the values come from the fake and were never compared with a PyBullet run
upstream draws the command, mass/friction and observation noise from numpy's default_rng; the fake uses Python's random.Random, so a seed gives different values on the two
no rendering: render() and the 640x480 rgb_array frame are not modelled, and the bridge does not bind cap.world.render.v1
the upstream package needs pybullet>=3.2, gymnasium>=0.29 and numpy; the package imports none of them, and no sim backend is declared because no gymnasium id is registered for YertleEnv
no physical Yertle is modelled and no hardware run was made

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
